# System Qt6 in CI is not built with -fsanitize=thread, so TSan cannot see
# the synchronization in QCoreApplication::postEvent / event-queue mutex.
# This makes every queued signal/slot delivery look like a race -- either on
# the QMetaCallEvent itself (caught by called_from_lib) or on the by-value
# arguments copied into our slot via the moc-generated dispatcher (caught by
# the qt_static_metacall pattern, which only matches the moc shim).
called_from_lib:libQt6Core.so
# Qt Gui's internal threads hand allocations to each other the same way.
called_from_lib:libQt6Gui.so
race:qt_static_metacall
race:QtPrivate::QMetaTypeForType

# CalcWorker is torn down via the standard Qt deleteLater + QThread::finished
# idiom: the worker's destructor runs on the worker thread when its event loop
# flushes deferred-delete events, and the happens-before chain back to earlier
# main-thread invokeMethod calls passes through uninstrumented Qt internals.
# The destructor itself is = default with no body, so there is no real shared
# state to race on -- only the object-lifetime sync that TSan cannot observe.
race:Avogadro::QtGui::CalcWorker::~CalcWorker

# BackgroundFileFormatTest tears its worker down the same way. The main
# thread's quit() is what triggers the deferred delete, but that ordering
# passes through the same uninstrumented Qt event queue. The destructor only
# deletes m_format, which was used on the worker thread alone.
race:Avogadro::QtGui::BackgroundFileFormat::~BackgroundFileFormat

# Qt6 on Linux uses glib's main loop by default, which wakes worker threads
# via an eventfd. Synchronization happens through the kernel fd, which TSan
# doesn't model; glib itself isn't instrumented either.
called_from_lib:libglib-2.0.so

# Surfaces' EDT runs QtConcurrent::run -> nested QtConcurrent::map, and hands
# results back through QFutureWatcher. QThreadPool/QFutureInterface sync inside
# uninstrumented libQt6Core (futex QMutex), so every hand-off (main -> worker,
# outer task -> inner map workers, worker -> main) looks like a race. We cannot
# match QtConcurrent frames: every pool-thread stack has them, and that would
# hide all pool races. ~MapKernel is the teardown vs forThreadFunction case.
# Trade-off: this also blinds TSan to a real race inside the EDT fill itself.
# That race is prevented by construction (x-slab partitioning: each task writes
# only voxels of its own indexX) and checked by the exact voxel comparison in
# surfacestest.cpp. With a TSan-instrumented Qt, remove these entries first.
race:Avogadro::QtPlugins::Surfaces::calculateEDT
race:Avogadro::QtPlugins::Surfaces::performEDTStep
race:~MapKernel

# Qt from install-qt-action is not TSan-instrumented and ships without symbols.
# libQt6Gui converts and scales large QImages on its own thread pool
# (QThread::start from inside libQt6Gui): a buffer allocated on the main thread
# is then copied and freed on those workers, and the hand-off synchronizes
# inside uninstrumented Qt, so it looks like a race. Every racing frame sits in
# libQt6Gui (seen when dialogs are shown by the smoke tests' actions). This
# mirrors the called_from_lib:libQt6Core.so stance above and the
# leak:libQt6Gui.so entry in lsan-suppressions.txt.
# Trade-off: TSan no longer sees accesses made by libQt6Gui itself; accesses
# made by our own instrumented code are still checked.
called_from_lib:libQt6Gui.so
# GaussianSetConcurrent has the same QtConcurrent::map + QFutureWatcher
# hand-offs: the GUI thread builds the tools, work items and cube before the
# map starts, and frees the cube after finished() arrives. Both orderings pass
# through uninstrumented libQt6Core. The kernel is instantiated on our own
# GaussianShell type, so these match only orbital/density workers and the
# map's own start-up, not other pool work. Trade-off: TSan is also blind to a
# real race with these workers (e.g. the basis set changing mid-calculation);
# x-slab partitioning keeps the workers' own writes disjoint.
race:QtConcurrent::IterateKernel<QList<Avogadro::QtGui::GaussianShell>
race:QtConcurrent::map<QList<Avogadro::QtGui::GaussianShell>

# MeshGenerator is a QThread that fills a mesh the plugin owns; the plugin
# publishes it once finished() arrives and isRunning() is false, which the
# QThread's own (futex) mutex orders. The molecule frees it much later, and
# TSan sees no edge back from the generator thread unless the GUI thread
# happened to be woken through Qt's eventfd. Match only the free, so that the
# generator's reads of the cube stay visible; a mesh freed while still in use
# would be a use-after-free, which the ASan job covers.
race:Avogadro::Core::Mesh::~Mesh
